name_reason: Already compliant: fd2_ game prefix + descriptor 'fill_palette_blink_pattern' accurately describes the action (fills a caller buffer with a 6-entry palette-index blink pattern). The '6byte' suffix is a structural dimension (the loop writes exactly 6 contiguous bytes, i<6), not a Ghidra address residue -- 0x33fc1 bears no relation to 6, and the value is meaningful domain semantics, so it is preserved.
purpose: Fills a 6-byte caller buffer with a contiguous, anchor-based palette-index sequence used for double-buffered blink/highlight effects.
logic_summary: base = input_index & 0xF8 (floor to a multiple of 8). bump = (input_index % 8 > 3) ? 2 : 0. for i in 0..5: out[i] = (uint8)(base + bump + i). The +2 bump shifts the anchor when the low 3 bits of input_index fall in the high half (4-7), mapping the two halves of an 8-step cycle onto palette pair A (offset 0) vs pair B (offset 2) -- a double-buffered blink swap. Binary uses signed IDIV by 8 for the remainder; for the documented 0..255 byte domain this equals the unsigned remainder, so `int % 8` reproduces it. Sum is truncated in an 8-bit register, mirrored by the uint8 store.

params.name: input_index
params.semantics: Anchor index value (byte domain 0..255). Used two ways: input_index & 0xF8 gives the base (floor to multiple of 8); input_index % 8 selects the +2 bump when the low 3 bits are in [4,7].
params.reason: Descriptive and accurate; no address residue; matches body usage as the per-call anchor index.

params.name: output_buffer_addr
params.semantics: Destination buffer address; the loop writes 6 consecutive bytes (out[0..5]) starting here.
params.reason: Descriptive and accurate; clearly identifies the write target; no address residue.

returns.semantics: No return value; the result is the 6 bytes written into the caller-provided buffer.
